title: Cilia
body: Cilin has to be secreted. It bristles the whole surface, and both the density of the coat and the length of the hairs follow how strongly it is expressed. The ciliary motor has to sit in the membrane. A position tag makes the cilia around that site row the cell in the direction the site names.

Motors on opposite sites cancel. A motor with no position tag coats every site and flaps the hairs without a direction, so the coat stirs and does not push. Like flagella, cilia stop when the ATP pool is empty.
